searchText: <@!425279588009246720> thanks for the explanation. I'm planning to dig into the binary trie spec tomorrow and am planning to make the same suggestion there (assuming it also seems ot make sense). Assumign there is no strong opposition... I'll circle back in a few days and maybe we can update the spec to remove the RLP 😁 I'm definitely a big fan of removing RLP And making sure that the code is put into a *simple binary tree* (it's possible that the existing binary state tree spec actually special-cases into a regular binary tree when the keys are all contiguous, would be good to see if that's true) Once <@!259648573401071617> is back next week, we'll propose a new version (probably next Friday or so) based on the "index-based approach" (see rationale), without RLP, and likely using a self contained tree specification (not relying on any external spec, like binarification or the YP). <@!364458974906548225> if you have the time please read the rationale, it lists a lot of different ideas/options we have considered and why we chose the specific one for this given version.
